_doc: Known, itemised, ACCEPTED clipping for generated hero assets. An entry records that a line's rendered right edge exceeds its asset's logical width, names the exact substring the reader never sees, and states the condition under which the clipping would be restored to full visibility. Read by tools/demo/audit.mjs.
_not_a_blessing: This ledger exists so clipping can never again be SILENT. It is not a place to retire a defect. A line the manifest classifies as kind 'verdict' carries the demonstration's proof and is REJECTED from this ledger outright by the auditor; such a line must have its clipping actually removed. Any clipped line absent from this ledger fails --strict, so omission is not a way to pass either.
_measurement: Right edge is computed on the renderer's fixed monospace grid (content origin x + character count x advance, both read from the asset itself), so it is deterministic and font-independent.
_currently_empty: No asset clips. The renderer fits each asset's logical width to its widest line (tools/demo/gen-svg.mjs), so a line cannot be cut off by the viewport, and the two guard-hero entries that lived here were retired as stale rather than carried — this ledger records CLIPPING, and there is none to record. Their stated blocker — that zero clipping needed 1390px while an 11px phone glyph permitted at most 488px — was not dissolved, only separated: the width side is satisfied (nothing is cut off) while the glyph side still binds and is still missed.
_corrected_2026-08-06: The two sentences that stood here were false and are withdrawn, not silently rewritten. They read: 'the full-size asset anchor, not the inline rendering, is the reader's path to legible proof, so the phone-glyph floor no longer binds and the interval is not empty.' Both halves are wrong against the live tree. (1) No anchor to a full-size SVG exists: the README's hero anchor resolves to .github/assets/hero-capture.txt, the raw captured log — that text capture, not a full-size asset, is the reader's path to untruncated proof. (2) The 11px phone-glyph floor still binds and is still missed: scripts/measure-hero-fold.py exits 2 with four glyph-floor failures, and the README's hero-glyph row publishes 7.55px at a 1280px viewport and 3.76px at 390px against that floor, with hero-legibility published as 'partial' for exactly that reason. The retirement of the two entries is nonetheless correct on a different ground, stated above: a missed glyph floor is scaled-down text, not lost text, so it belongs in that published disclosure and not in this clipping ledger.
